title: GECO: evidence, intervention and recovery
notes: Open with the practical question: when a system reports that it delivered something, what evidence would persuade us? GECOv6 is a research package, not an approved medical device. All numerical units are research model units. The IIT Patna rig is a proposal pending construction and measurement.
paragraphs: A reproducible simulation and methods study
Corrected prediction · matched comparisons · a measurable saline rig
IEEE-style research seminar | team and author details to be completed

title: The motivating question
notes: Explain the three verbs: request, permit and emit. They name different events. Then explain the tradeoff in ordinary language: stopping a malfunction can help, but a stop that lasts too long also has a cost. Do not suggest the simulations establish patient benefit.
paragraphs: A permitted command and an accepted command do not prove fluid reached the outlet.
A monitor can reduce unwanted delivery while also interrupting wanted delivery.
The study measures both sides of intervention, including return to service.

title: The evidence boundary
notes: Trace the six boxes in order. A digital acknowledgment belongs near authorization; it must not be used as a substitute for emitted fluid. The experiment distinguishes local mass evidence from the network report, which matters when only the report is masked.
caption: Each link has its own value, timestamp, authority and possible failure.

title: The contribution to test
notes: The contribution is the accountable method and evidence separation. Prior work already includes insulin safety monitors, physiological models and gravimetric pump assessment. Do not claim the first digital twin, first safety monitor or first mass-sensing pump.
paragraphs: An auditable chain from observations and commands to measurement and response.
A comparison that matches what each practical method can observe and control.
A release that preserves failures, censored recovery and model-domain violations.

title: Thirty-minute prediction error
notes: Embedded chart values are rounded to 6 decimalplaces from the linked exact source; labels display 1 decimal. title: Prediction findings and limits
notes: Bootstrap intervals describe variation across these participants, not an external population guarantee. The median empirical 95% forecast coverage was 95.82%, ranging 87.50–98.92%. Good median coverage conceals poor coverage for individual participants.24/31 fits approached parameter bounds; do not infer physiological identifiability.

title: Faults and observation assumptions
notes: The factor 2 is applied before quantization, gain, noise and dribble, so do not say exactly twice the emitted dose. Masked network reports do not compromise the independent local mass cutoff. This makes the model of remaining trusted evidence narrower than total sensor compromise.

title: The six primary response arms
notes: Full and simple differ in temporal aggregation as well as physiological input. Their difference alone cannot identify the incremental value of physiology. The separate exploratory fasting supplement adds a mass-CUSUM-only arm to address this component question.

title: Response and recovery states
notes: Trip timing is measured at the end of the triggering interval; stop effect is at the next interval in the primary model. Cooldown starts at that interval boundary. Supervised checks require current CGM and six quiet local readings; probe aggregate mass must meet the specified tolerance. The state before emission determines latch exposure. Guards remain active throughout probation.
caption: No catch-up delivery. Manual release and supervised recovery are separate comparisons.

title: Primary experiment outcome
notes: Execution success means the specified software ran; it does not mean the model was physiologically valid.2,108 of 4,608 main runs had domain violations, all in the Hovorka branch. This is a central limitation, not a footnote.
paragraphs: 5,184 runs completed without execution exceptions.
The full monitor did not show consistent superiority to the simpler monitor.
Independent review checked every full trace and recomputed core outcomes; all domain violations were retained.

It is not an external cohort, therapy validation or a retrospective repair of primary results. The final results slide is generated only from reviewed supplemental output.

New fasting parameter vectors and noise seeds; actuator-aware basal compensation.

title: Fasting supplement: validity and false stops
notes: Post-primary exploratory design; 16 new test parameter vectors per plant,2 new noise seeds,8 conditions and 4 supervised arms. Analytically selected actuator-aware fasting commands avoid the primary meal-driven domain failures. This does not validate meal responses or actual physiology. No unit or unsuccessful result was excluded. The original family still recorded 18,648 remote-action clamp slots, including 51 in clean runs; passing the screen is not physiological validation.
values: Declared screens passed; false stops remain

title: Full versus mass CUSUM: benefits and costs
notes: These contrasts compare the added physiological rule together with its separately clean-calibrated threshold: full 2.8330 versus mass-only 2.5291. They do not isolate physiology at an identical numerical threshold. The full detector can gain sensitivity when observations support it and incur costs when CGM is biased. These four examples do not replace the complete six-contrast table and all 8 condition results.
caption: Exploratory fasting comparison. Less excess under a combined fault; more deficit under biased CGM.

title: What can be claimed now
notes: The paper is ready for team review as a simulation/methods manuscript. Publication acceptance is a reviewer decision. The scientific value includes the negative result: added monitor complexity did not earn an unconditional superiority claim.
paragraphs: A reproducible simulation and methods contribution with explicit evidence boundaries.
A corrected prediction comparison that favors simpler candidates on these records.
A documented intervention tradeoff and a physical validation protocol ready for the team.

title: What remains before submission
notes: Hardware is not automatically required for every simulation paper. A submission can proceed on a carefully scoped simulation contribution if the venue accepts that scope. Hardware accuracy, physical cessation and clinical safety claims need the corresponding evidence; the manuscript does not make them.
paragraphs: Authors must approve the claims, contributions, references and assistance disclosure.
Choose the IEEE venue, then apply its exact scope, length and submission requirements.
Physical measurement claims remain amber until IIT Patna supplies reviewed evidence.

title: The research story
notes: Close by returning to the opening question. The contribution is more persuasive when the audience can see what would falsify it. Explain that future saline measurements can either support or challenge the assumed sensor and actuator behavior.
paragraphs: We asked whether a monitor can connect permission with credible delivery evidence.
We repaired the testable implementation and challenged it against simpler alternatives.
The strongest result is a transparent method, a bounded claim and a concrete next experiment.
